spec.description: Local inference in nav-pilot alpha: who uses it, what they send there, and whether the server comes up. Every query uses sum_over_time, not increase(): all runs on a machine share a series and start at their own 1, so increase() gives 0. Each sample is what is new since the process's last export, so the sum counts each run once.
How many ran at least one local session in the range. The denominator for everything else here.
spec.title: Machines running locally

spec.description: One session is one client run with a local worker available, counted when the client exits.
spec.title: Sessions

spec.description: Total tasks the main agent actually sent to the local model.
spec.title: Tasks sent locally

spec.description: The panel that decides whether the alpha widens. See the breakdown below for why the number is what it is: a zero does not mean the same thing in the two cases.
spec.title: Share of sessions without dispatch

spec.description:
The one graph worth building the dashboard for. saw_traffic=true means the client reached the worker and chose not to use it: a verdict on the model. saw_traffic=false means the connection never got through, which is our fault, not the model's. Without this split a zero is three different things reported as one.

WAITING FOR DATA: saw_traffic was added after the alpha shipped, so the panel is empty until people upgrade. Empty is correct here: a zero we cannot interpret is worse than no line.
spec.title: Sessions without dispatch, by whether the client saw the worker

spec.description: Distribution, never mean: most sessions send nothing and a few send a lot, and an average of the two describes no real session. The buckets are subtracted from each other, so each bar is sessions in exactly that interval.
spec.title: Tasks per session

spec.description: opencode runs the model as a subagent under a cloud agent; Copilot CLI runs the whole session locally.
spec.title: Sessions per interval, by client

spec.description: What the guard in front of the local model did in sessions with local_dispatch balanced or aggressive. deny_* are things it stopped; dispatched_after_deny still ended in a dispatch; verify_nudge is the reminder when the local model is done and no build or test has run since; create_retry* is follow-up after it created a new file.
spec.title: Dispatch guard, by outcome

spec.description:
p50 and p95 for starts that actually came up. The filter outcome="ready" is not decoration: a start that times out contributes ten minutes, and a p95 without the filter measures the failures, not the wait.

WAITING FOR DATA: outcome arrived after the previous release, so the panel fills once people upgrade.
spec.title: Time to ready

spec.description:
ready, failed or interrupted. Until this existed only successful starts were recorded, so the slow tail was missing by construction.

WAITING FOR DATA: outcome arrived after the previous release and fills as people upgrade. From the same release autostart is counted too, which is the usual way in; before, the histogram only measured starts someone typed by hand.
spec.title: How starts ended

spec.description: Should be one. More means someone runs something we have not measured.
